items.justification: Data erasure functionality versus notification of security updates.
Uniqueness of security parameters versus internal risk reporting culture.
Publishing the support period versus pre-release security testing.
Runtime input validation versus a pre-build requirements and risk assessment.
Both govern end of life but pursue different objectives: hardware replaceability versus secure disposal of data and configuration.
Credential change mechanism versus usage and configuration guidance.
User setup guidance versus assurance over external risk owners.
Both are transparency duties toward the user, on different subject matter: support lifetime versus how data is used and stored.
Cryptographic confidentiality in transit versus least-privilege permissions between systems.
Both require changes to a system to be tracked, A through version control in development and B through an audit log of configuration and prompt changes.
Both observe the running system for security-relevant state, A by alerting on detected tampering and B by monitoring internal states.
Memory access control versus incident management and recovery planning.
Authenticated configuration change versus justification for undocumented components.
Tamper-resistant device identity versus disclosure of data handling practices.
Resilience to network and power outage versus monitoring internal model states.
Both require restoration to a known good working state after disruption; A adds continued local operation during network loss.
Model designation labelling and security-relevant system documentation are different objectives that together let a stakeholder identify and assess what they hold.
Both apply access control to protect system internals, A at the hardware memory level and B across APIs, models and pipelines.
Cryptographic verification of updates and due diligence on external components are distinct objectives that together establish trust in incoming code.
Support period publication versus human oversight capability.
Both apply least functionality: A enables only the software services required for operation, B grants only the permissions required for functionality and adds a risk assessment.
Per-device parameter uniqueness versus secure software supply chain process.
Isolability of unsupportable devices versus threat analysis and risk management.
Setup guidance versus pre-release security assessment.
Support period publication versus supplier due diligence.
Both work toward updates actually reaching and being applied by users, A through ease of application and B through provision and delivery.
Both protect the integrity of software assets, A by detecting unauthorized change and B by authenticating and version-controlling assets.
Hardware replaceability versus involvement of Data Custodians in requirements setting.
Both mandate confidentiality protection for sensitive assets, A for security parameters in transit and B for training data and model weights.
Update integrity verification versus vulnerability disclosure policy.
Recording justifications for non-applicable provisions versus behavioural monitoring.
Publishing replacement support versus secure coding training for developers.
Key lifecycle management versus communicating unresolved threats down the supply chain.
Cryptographic protection of communications versus update notification.
Credential change mechanism versus vulnerability disclosure policy.
Physical interface exposure versus software supply chain process.
Secure development practice and access-control evaluation are distinct objectives that jointly determine whether the built system is defensible.
Credential change mechanism versus component justification.
Hardware replaceability versus advance notice of model updates.
Both require confidentiality protection proportionate to sensitivity, A for personal data in transit and B for training data and model weights.
